compiled_state.description:
## Context

S1 produces a rewritten below-horizon baseline on a shadow clone. This story builds the
**publish-swap** that would replace the published `tickets` history with that baseline — as a
per-backend adapter over one precondition ("replace iff the remote is unchanged since T0, else
abort+retry") — plus the rollback re-convergence design. It STOPS before executing any real swap.

## Scope

- **git ref remotes** (bare/GitHub/Gerrit): swap via `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/tickets:T0` (old→new ref CAS).
- **S3 `git-remote-s3` backend (ADR 0093):** there is NO atomic ref CAS. The helper stores one git bundle per push, and the non-interactive auto-doctor (`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`) folds divergent heads by lossless 2-parent merges and NEVER discards a head — so a normally-pushed rewrite would be MERGED BACK (resurrected). Implement an EXCLUSIVE offline bundle-set replacement under the per-ref push-lock: assert the head set equals T0 (the CAS precondition), back up the bundle set to a rollback key prefix, write ONE rewritten bundle, delete the originals — bypassing the auto-doctor.
- **Rollback re-convergence (plan-review advisory #4):** design and document the path for clients that already reconciled onto the rewritten baseline (new SHAs) BEFORE a rollback — after rollback they point at a baseline graph the remote no longer has. Specify how they re-converge (e.g. treat the restored pre-reclaim ref as authoritative and force-override per the C3 stale-clone protocol).

## Out of scope

Executing a swap against any real `tickets` remote — that is a separate human go/no-go after the S3
dry-run. Everything here is validated against throwaway remotes/fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The git-ref adapter swaps via `--force-with-lease` and ABORTS (no write) when the remote moved since T0, verified on a throwaway bare remote.
- [ ] The S3 adapter performs an exclusive push-locked bundle-set replacement that asserts the T0 head set, backs up bundles to a rollback prefix, writes one rewritten bundle, deletes originals, and does NOT trigger an auto-doctor merge — verified on a fake-S3 fixture.
- [ ] A backup ref / rollback bundle prefix is captured before the first destructive step in each adapter.
- [ ] The rollback re-convergence path for already-reconciled clients is documented and covered by a reconvergence fixture (a client on the rewritten baseline is force-overridden back onto the restored ref).
- [ ] [non-codebase] No real `tickets` remote is swapped by this story.

## Portability

Both adapters use either core-git ref primitives or the store's existing S3 seam; no single-CI-provider dependence.
